subs.text: Book eleven.
The Kingdom of the Dead.
Scene one.
The Blood Pit Opens.
The ship came to deep-flowing Ocean's edge, to the land of the Cimmerians, wrapped in mist and cloud,
where the shining sun never looks down.
By milk and honey, wine and white barley, I call you, nations of the dead —
but stand off from the blood!
The dead gather in multitudes, crying around the blood.
Odysseus waits for Tiresias before allowing any other shade to drink.

subs.text: Scene two.
Elpenor Asks for Burial.
Elpenor's unburied ghost approaches first and Odysseus weeps in recognition.
His roof fall and begs for funeral rites on Aeaea.
Burn me with all my armor and heap a mound by the grey sea, for an unlucky man that men to come may know of.
And plant above it the oar I pulled while I lived among my friends —
will you do this for me?
All this I will do, poor Elpenor —
I will leave nothing undone.
When I stand again on Aeaea, fire and mound and oar shall be yours.

scenes.title: Tiresias Names the Cost
scenes.card: The prophet Tiresias warns that the crew must not touch the Sun god's cattle, and that Odysseus will reach home alone.

subs.text: Scene three.
Tiresias Names the Cost.
The blood is dark and sweet.
Now I know you, son of Laertes.
You seek a honey-sweet homecoming, but a god will make it bitter.
The Earthshaker holds his grudge —
you blinded the son he loved, and he does not forget.
Hear me, all of you:
when you come to Thrinacia, where the cattle of the Sun graze, keep your hands from those herds.
Harm them, and I foretell ruin for ship and crew —
and if you yourself escape, you come home late and wretched, on a stranger's ship, with every companion lost.
Tiresias foretells Odysseus's lone return, the suitors' punishment, and a final inland journey carrying an oar.
After a distant sacrifice to Poseidon, death will come gently in old age.

scenes.title: Anticleia and the Three Embraces
scenes.card: Odysseus meets his mother, who died of longing for him; three times he tries to hug her, and his arms pass through.

subs.text: Scene four.
Anticleia and the Three Embraces.
Come, mother —
drink of the blood and know me.
It is I, alive, your son.
Odysseus describes Penelope's fidelity, Telemachus's position, and Laertes's isolated grief.
No sickness took you, then.
It was longing —
longing for me, for my counsels and my gentleness —
that stole the honey of your life.
My going killed you, mother.
Odysseus tries three times to embrace her, but his arms pass through the shade.

subs.text: Scene five.
The Heroines of the Past.
Odysseus lets a succession of famous women drink and identify their lineages.
Tyro tells of Poseidon and your river-born sons.
Then came Antiope and Alcmene, Megara and sorrowing Epicaste, Chloris, Leda, Iphimedeia, Phaedra, Ariadne —
Maera, Clymene, and hateful Eriphyle, each with her story at her lips.
And the trench became a living book of mothers:
desire and birth, crime and death, line after line of the world's begetting.

subs.text: Scene six.
Agamemnon's Warning.
Agamemnon drinks and tells how Aegisthus and Clytemnestra murdered him at a feast.
He heard Cassandra's dying cry above him as he lay.
And the wife turned away —
she would not even draw down his eyelids as he went to the house of Death.
So take his warning, Odysseus:
put in to your own land secretly, not openly.
Show your full mind to no woman, not even a faithful wife —
the day of trusting them is done.
About Orestes, but Odysseus has no news?

scenes.title: Achilles Chooses Life in Retrospect
scenes.card: Achilles says death holds no glory, asks after his family, and strides off rejoicing to hear his son fought bravely.

subs.text: Scene seven.
Achilles Chooses Life in Retrospect.
Then came the shade of Achilles, son of Peleus, and with him Patroclus and brave Antilochus —
and Ajax, standing apart.
Achilles, no man was ever more blessed, nor will be:
alive we honored you like a god, and here you rule with power among the dead.
Do not grieve at dying —
you of all men.
Would you hear of Peleus, and of your son Neoptolemus?
Of your father I know nothing —
but of the boy I can speak truly, for I myself brought him from Scyros to the war.
In council he spoke first and best;
in battle he never lagged in the crowd, but charged far ahead.
When we crouched inside the wooden horse the other chiefs wept and trembled —
he only gripped his sword-hilt and begged me to let him leap out.
And he took his prize and sailed home unwounded.
Achilles strides away rejoicing.
Only Ajax, son of Telamon, stood apart, angry still over the arms of Achilles that Odysseus won.
Soft words were called to him —
but the shade answered nothing, and went away in silence among the dead.

scenes.title: Judges, Punishments, and Flight
scenes.card: Odysseus sees the punished dead and famous heroes, until the crowding ghosts frighten him back to his ship.

subs.text: Scene eight.
Judges, Punishments, and Flight.
Minos with the golden scepter, judging the dead —
and huge Orion, herding before him the ghosts of the beasts he killed on lonely hills.
Tityus stretched under the tearing vultures, Tantalus thirsting with water at his chin,
Sisyphus shouldering his pitiless stone.
I am only shadow —
the man himself feasts among the deathless gods and holds fair-ankled Hebe.
But you, poor wretch —
do you too haul some such doom as I hauled beneath the sun?
Son of Zeus I was, and still I slaved for a lesser man, who sent me down even here to drag away the hound.
The dead crowd closer and Odysseus fears Persephone may send a monster.
Heracles's phantom retreats to the ship and sails back across Ocean.
